text:
maria_gonzalez: quick heads-up — ran an nsys capture on the ~5k req workload and saw a perf regression on the kv cache hotpath. attaching snippets below.

maria_gonzalez: top-level observation: kernel switch count jumped ~20% at 0.8s mark, and wall time per-request increased ~12%. suspect we introduced extra serialization when cache miss handling hits the small-batch path.

alex_park: can you paste the nsys timeline screenshot or export?

maria_gonzalez: perf-ci uploaded the trace: https://perf-artifacts.internal/2367891234/nsys/trace.qdrep 

perf-ci: artifact: https://perf-artifacts.internal/2367891234/nsys/trace.qdrep (uploaded by perf-ci) :white_check_mark:

jordan_lee: skimmed the qdrep — there's a cluster of tiny cudaLaunchKernel calls right after the KV lookup stage. they look like tiny, inefficient kernels instead of the fused path.

samuel_han: that matches my local repro. when batching falls to <4 tokens/req the kernel selector prefers the safe kernel which has a pre/post barrier causing CPU <-> GPU sync points.

alex_park: hmm — our NVTX ranges currently mark "kv_lookup" as a single span, but we don't instrument the internal branches (miss vs hit). so contributor attribution is lost. i'm worried we might be aggregating missed-hit cost into the wrong kernel.

maria_gonzalez: proposal: add short NVTX ranges around the miss handling and around the cache-hit fast-path. something like:

```cpp
// pseudo
nvtxRangePushA("rt.kv.req.<short-id>.hit");
// fast path code
nvtxRangePop();

nvtxRangePushA("rt.kv.req.<short-id>.miss");
// miss handling code (IO / kernel launch / fallback)
nvtxRangePop();
```

jordan_lee: i like the scoped detail but worried about label cardinality — we can't have full request ids in names, perf tools blow up. use stable short-id or bucketed labels: e.g., `rt.kv.hit`, `rt.kv.miss.sync`, `rt.kv.miss.async` and then attach a `nvtxPushEx` payload with an integer span_id for correlating per-request.

samuel_han: yes — add an attribute integer. nvtxRangeStartEx supports `nvtxPayload_t` where we can stash a 64-bit span id. then perfetto can map the integer to a request in postprocessing.

alex_park: concrete naming suggestion: `rt.req>kv:hit`, `rt.req>kv:miss.sync`, `rt.req>kv:miss.kernellaunch`. small, consistent tokens are easier to grep. include `rt` prefix to separate from other subsystems.

maria_gonzalez: also saw multiple overlapping ranges marked as `kv_cache` and `batch_dispatch` — overlap made it look like kernel cost was inside batch_dispatch but it was actually kernel launch latency. so we need strict non-overlapping lexical spans per thread. push/pop ordering must be consistent even on error paths.

jordan_lee: +1 on ordered spans. also recommend adding a `rt.batch.size` nvtx marker at batch boundaries (not per request) so we can join batch size timeline with kernel timelines. small command example: `nvtxMarkA("rt.batch.size=3")` at enqueue time.

samuel_han: aside: can we add a lightweight sampling tracer that emits compact CSV of span_id,kernel_name,start_ns,end_ns to speed up analysis for large traces? full nsys is heavy to parse each time.

perf-ci: perf artifact for quick csv extractor: https://perf-tools.internal/trace-summarizer/2367891234.csv (auto-generated)

maria_gonzalez: thanks. next steps i propose:
- implement scoped miss/hit NVTX ranges with short token names and integer payloads (sam will own)
- ensure push/pop ordering is consistent on all branches (alex will audit)
- add `rt.batch.size` marks at enqueue and dispatch points (jordan will add)
- run nsys capture on canary and compare kernel switch counts + per-request wall time (maria will run)

alex_park: noted. i'll add a tiny helper RAII NVTX guard in tracing.h so devs won't forget pop on exceptions. example:

```cpp
struct NvtxGuard { nvtxRangeId_t id; NvtxGuard(const char* n) { id=nvtxRangeStartA(n); } ~NvtxGuard(){ nvtxRangeEnd(id); } };
```

jordan_lee: will add `rt.batch.size` marks and a small perf-test that hits edge-case batch sizes (1..8).

samuel_han: i'll prototype payload-based span ids and CSV exporter. plan to tag each span with a compact 32-bit id and emit to a ringbuffer on CPU side. then post-process to correlate with kernel names.

maria_gonzalez: if everyone is aligned, i'll spin up a canary job for the regression bucket and schedule a 30-min profiling window tomorrow 09:00 PT.

devx-bot: reminder: please add a short PR description linking the perf trace and include the `perf: nvtx` label when you open the change.

alex_park: ping if you need help with the RAII wrapper — i'll sketch the PR today.

jordan_lee: thanks — will send initial batch marks PR by EOD.

maria_gonzalez: thanks all. saving csv and qdrep in the incident folder: /artifacts/2367891234/ for follow-up.
